title: The incident record, its three operations, its record code and its right are not in the sources, and the legacy permission table conflicts with the technical specification
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-017); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.28); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T3.1, T3.2, T5.1, T6.1, appendix T-A); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql; _work/msr/context/P4.md
description: Five values of this key are not in the sources and one of them is a conflict. (1) There is no incident entity anywhere: not in TSD P4 v3 T3.1, not in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 and not in the Physical Schema v6, and the ownership map gives P4 five tables, none of them an incident, so the record has no table and its shape must be fixed. (2) The three operations that record an incident - open, closure and read - are not in appendix T-A of TSD P4 v3, which lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 with no incident path, and the legacy story names only the rule-version endpoints of another story. (3) The record code that marks a step in the local decision-record chain, the field-level shape of a step inside an entry and the format of the incident id are not stated. (4) The screen that carries the incident is not named: the legacy screen table gives SCR-39 Rules and parameters and SCR-41 Delegation of authority, and neither is an incident screen. (5) The detection source is not declared: FSD P4 v3 A2.28.2 names Log Analytics as an integration point and TSD P4 v3 T5.1 declares only INT-21 and INT-22 for P4, so no interface from the observability platform to this service exists. (6) The conflict: the legacy permission checks table gives Rules and parameters C to RW-COE and A to RW-RISK, FSD P4 v3 A2.28.3.3 makes the platform administrator the primary role, and TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-PLATADM CRUD in Platform administration and R only in Rules and parameters; R-PREC puts the Technical Specifications above the story master, so the path's right is Platform administration and the legacy letters are the rule-change right set of the same chapter.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E8-017 gives the story sentence, two generic ACs, a permission table (Rules and parameters C: RW-COE; A: RW-RISK), a data table naming decision_log_entry, rule_row and role, and the two rule-version endpoints; FSD P4 v3 A2.28 gives VR-P4-028-1, BR-P4-028, the role table, AC-P4-028-01 marked Written one epic ahead and two exception criteria, and no operation, no field and no state; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and T3.2 give role, permission, delegation_limit, masking_rule and role_conflict with LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-SCOPE and the letters, and T6.1 gives RW-PLATADM CRUD and RW-SECADM CRUDA in Platform administration with RW-AUDIT R; appendix T-A.1 lists no incident operation; the Logical Data Model and the Physical Schema contain no incident table or column; the context pack rows for P4 name four REST operations (GET /admin/access-log, GET /admin/roles, GET /me/session, POST /admin/break-glass-grants), no event and one job JOB-18
proposed: Build the incident as a record of rwb-access and not as a table: two entries of the local decision-record chain of DP-03 per incident, one for DETECTED and HELD on the open and one for FIXED, RECORDED and REPORTED on the closure, each in the transaction of its idempotency row, with the parameters version in force carried on the entry through DP-06. Fix the three paths on the access base in RWB-P4-E8017-CON, fix the five step names from the legacy criterion's own words and the two states OPEN and CLOSED, fix the held-area lists to LOV-CAPABILITY, the letters and LOV-SCOPE, and read the right as Platform administration C, U and R of TSD P4 v3 T6.1 rather than the legacy Rules and parameters letters. Keep the record code and the incident-id format open at D1 and settle them with the ledger owner and audit. Leave the incident screen to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the detection to RWB-PLT-OBS, and enforce nothing on the other services here.
